approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local molecular genetic algorithm with a Bayesian purchase step. It keeps one bounded population of the sixty-four best-scoring molecules observed so far in the current session, ordered strictly by score with arrival order breaking ties. Breeding parents are drawn from that population with a strong preference for its top score quantiles, a molecule is never paired with itself, and each announcement builds a fresh field of 160 de novo candidates by connected-fragment crossover with an optional finishing edit, or by a one-to-three step walk of atom and bond mutations; every candidate must be a connected, canonically stable, previously unseen graph. A Gaussian process with a count-fingerprint generalized-Tanimoto kernel is refitted on every accepted score of the session, ten correlated function draws are taken over the whole fresh field, and the ten molecules sent for evaluation are the sampled maxima picked one at a time without replacement. After three announcements with no improvement of the best molecule the purchase is restricted to the forty highest posterior means until an improving batch restores the full field. Accepted scores enter the archive and compete for the population immediately, so an accepted offspring can breed in the very next announcement. An earlier Child in this lineage removed an admission rule that had rejected candidates introducing unusual sulfur environments relative to their own parents, keeping its classifier as a passive measurement.
approach.novelty: In the Parent the breeding memory and the breeding source are the same single store, so every line of descent in a session passes through one ranked population and one sampler, and the lineage's own measurements show the paid stream collapsing into a few analogue families while the generated field stays varied. This Child splits that store into two independent lines of descent holding thirty-two records each - the same total capacity - seeded by dealing the initial records alternately down the score ranking. Each line retains only the purchases bred from its own members, draws both parents from inside itself, and generates exactly half of the unchanged 160-candidate field; nothing migrates between them and no record is ever held by both. The surrogate still learns from every accepted label of the session, the ten purchases are still priced and chosen jointly over the whole field with the same eligibility rule, and the session's best molecule is still read across both lines, so the only thing that changes is how many ancestries can survive and breed at once. Earlier attempts on this lineage to break the same concentration keyed retention on a molecule's structure inside the one store and failed because the records they protected ranked below anything the sampler would draw; here each line owns its sampler, so everything it keeps is reachable by construction. A session whose first productive family stalls now still has a second line that has been breeding independently since the start.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-f28be8ac3d12 passes the whole ancestry of a session through one global greedy top-64 population feeding one quantile parent sampler, and its own published measurement record prices that congestion. Macro mean 0.613802723974122 over the fifteen matched cells (seed macros 0.640211742526581/0.60208683374541/0.599109595650375, paired +0.006772407762991002 over Anchor n-cf8d309c06de at 0.607030316211131). Of its 4,350 purchases only 634 beat their own generating root, 3,510 were admitted as survivors, and only 2,459 of the 4,200 non-terminal products ever became the root of a later accepted purchase, so 1,741 paid products are terminal; 255 purchases improved the incumbent and realized incumbent-increment mass totals 6.079659193977185 (per-cell mean 0.4053106129318124; per-seed sums 2.158598157421355/1.967973613515504/1.953087423040328). Supply is not the scarce thing: all 435 announcements filled their 160-member field, with a maximum of 201 breeding attempts against the unchanged 50,000 bound and 89 restricted batches. The same concentration is measured more sharply on this loop's curated pair n-a6cb628fa07e/n-b5d3c2aee387 (3,563 of 4,350 purchases failing to beat their root, 2,911 non-terminal products never becoming roots, mean paid extension depth 0.57 falling to 0.36) and in n-9659e4138ba7, where within-batch generalized count similarity of generated fields fell 0.604677 to 0.497327 while the similarity of the purchases rose 0.713379 to 0.752586: the field stays varied and the paid stream collapses into few analogue families. Every earlier attempt to decongest it stayed inside that one store or its one sampler and lost endpoint score - class round-robin survival -0.029689809698780656 (n-28dc36ed5be7), whole-molecule niche-elite retention -0.047212619373212715 (n-e1a97c9e8713), persistent property-cell champions with uniform breeding -0.055186727444823 (n-37a4fc183d94) - and the recorded cause is access, not membership: what those rules protected was ranked below anything the single sampler reaches. The quantity never varied on this lineage is the number of independent lines of descent a session can carry, so one early analogue family that scores well captures the sampler for the rest of the session.

literature_review.conclusion: No new literature source is adopted and none is claimed. The frozen review r80-exhausted-axes-review is reused for the bottleneck it establishes - every single-component axis of this loop measured and closed, with the decision machinery's own structure left untested - and the knowledge tree supplies the design constraints: keep bounded greedy retention, the rank-weighted quantile draw and the immediate accepted-offspring-to-breeder edge intact inside each line, put retention inside the consumer's reachable ranks by giving each line its own sampler, and read the outcome on realized incumbent-increment mass rather than on delivered diversity.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: Under the recorded stagnation the ticket permits reuse of the frozen Search Policy review r80-exhausted-axes-review together with the recorded knowledge_basis in place of a new web search, and this intervention introduces no model, package, asset or external method: it reorganizes the Parent's own breeding memory with its own inherited laws. None of that review's four papers supplies the element used here - its trust-region, variance-reduced base-sample and coverage-calibration candidates belong to the other positions of the round and the review itself records the population partition as the untested structural axis. The evidence for this change is internal: the Parent's own purchase, root-beating, reuse-of-source and increment-mass counts, the curated pair measurement of the same concentration, and the three recorded single-store retention failures with their recorded cause.

hypothesis: Replace the single bounded breeding population of Evolution by two bounded populations of capacity 32 each - the inherited population_size 64 divided by the declared breeding_partitions 2 - preserving every inherited retention, sampling, operator, admission and allocation law inside each. At session start the inherited filtered, canonically deduplicated initial records are ordered by (-score, serial) and dealt alternately by score rank, rank r to population r mod 2, after which each population applies the inherited strict (-score, serial) greedy truncation at its own capacity. Each announcement keeps the inherited 160 admitted field members and their generation order; the field slot being filled fixes its source population as (number of already admitted members) mod 2, so population 0 writes the even slots and population 1 the odd slots and each supplies exactly 80 members. The first parent and, in the crossover branch, the partner are drawn by the inherited quantile rule with its rank weights, identical-parent exclusion and empty-group fallback from that one population only, with the inherited crossover share, finishing-edit probability, one-to-three call mutation walk, crossover-probability halving above forty member attempts, canonical identity admission, both duplicate scopes and the global refill and attempt bounds unchanged. Every product therefore has exactly one source population, recorded in its provenance. An accepted purchase is offered for retention only to the population of its generating parents and competes there by the same strict (-score, serial) order and capacity rule; the other population never sees it, and no record is retained by or bred from both. The accepted-label archive, the count-fingerprint Gaussian-process fit over every accepted label of the session, the correlated ten-row Thompson draw over the whole 160-member field with its stall-conditioned top-forty eligibility mask, its sequential masking and tie rules, the canonical identity and duplicate scopes, the serial counter, the refill and attempt limits and the session incumbent - the better head of the two populations by (-score, serial) - all stay global and unchanged. No migration rule, no third population and no capacity or share sweep is added.

finding_summary.headline: Two ancestry-disjoint breeding lines ran exactly as registered, but the global buy spent 88% of purchases on one line and the panel fell 0.0553
finding_summary.insights:
The campaign now knows that the number of independent breeding lines is not the binding quantity on this loop, and for the first time it knows why. The three earlier decongestion attempts on this host all failed with a recorded cause: what they protected ranked below anything the parent sampler would draw. This node removed that cause by construction - each line owns its sampler, so every record it retains is inside its own consumer's reach, and the receipts confirm that every one of the 87,714 offspring-breeding parent draws came from the drawing line's own store - and it still lost 0.055. The reason is that reachability by the breeder is not the scarce thing; purchase is. Both lines generated exactly half of every field, and the one global posterior-mean ranking then spent seven eighths of the oracle budget on one of them, widening its own advantage as the leading family accumulated the labels the surrogate learns from. A line that is never bought cannot become an independent ancestry however cleanly it is isolated.

Two further things are now measured rather than assumed. First, preserving total capacity is not preserving memory. The cap stayed at 64, but realized live occupancy averaged 45.7 records per announcement: the leading store sat at 29-32 of its 32 slots while the trailing store averaged 16.7 and ended as low as 7, because it was fed too rarely to fill. The working line therefore ran on a 32-record store where the Parent ran on a saturated 64-record one, and that halving is visible as more eviction, less reuse and narrower output - the most plausible route by which the increment mass was lost. Second, the usual alternative reading is closed before anyone proposes it: this is not a 'bought diversity, got no score' result. Scaffold coverage fell and purchase similarity rose, so the partition delivered both less progress and narrower chemistry. The Molecular report describes the same collapse from the chemistry side: the top of each objective's range is a single family decorated one atom at a time, with 85 of the 100 best molecules of one objective on a single scaffold, and the score gradient is often indifferent to the edit being made (identical scores for chloro, fluoro and bromo variants of the same core), so a large part of the budget bought no information at all.

What this result leaves open is the consumer, not the producer. The two candidate causes - an unpartitioned acquisition and a halved per-store capacity - were changed together by this single intervention, so this node cannot separate them, and nothing here prices a partition whose allocation is also partitioned, nor any other line count, capacity split, field share, migration rule or partition key. The method class this points at is a different allocation and ranking scheme rather than a different memory layout: an acquisition that reserves purchases per line (a portfolio or bandit allocation across lines, or per-line posterior ranking instead of one global posterior-mean rank over the pooled field), or a surrogate conditioned on line identity so a trailing line's candidates are not judged by a model dominated by the leading family's labels. The trajectories also show the limitation that no memory or allocation change can reach: proposals are single-atom relabellings of inherited cores, so the whole search is local refinement of a few scaffolds, and a proposal operator that can place a whole group or cyclise an existing amine in one move is a separate and still untested lever. Whether the partitioned-breeding approach deserves another position is the Search Policy's call on the scope of the approach; what is settled here is that ancestry isolation alone, with the buy left global, costs this host.
finding_summary.results:
The partition executed to the letter over the complete fifteen-cell panel. All 435 announcements report two populations of capacity 32, the ten supplied initial records dealt five and five by alternating score rank in every session, every 160-member field split exactly 80/80 by slot parity with zero shortfall and no recorded cause, and no truncation. Across 870 disjointness receipts there is not one shared identity, mislabelled member or over-capacity store, the live total never exceeds 64, and cross-population pairings are zero over 81,492 breeding attempts, 69,600 pooled candidates and 4,350 purchases; the hardest work any announcement needed was 285 breeding attempts against an unchanged bound of 50,000 (the Parent's hardest was 201). The global half of the loop is untouched and measurably so: the surrogate refits on the whole session archive at every announcement (10, 20, ... 290 labels in all fifteen cells), all 160 candidates are priced jointly by the inherited ten correlated rows with the inherited posterior-mean rank rule at every one of the 4,350 selection positions, the stall mask restricted 93 announcements to the top forty against the Parent's 89, both duplicate scopes and canonical identity admission still run on every candidate, the sulfur classifier is still passive (218 'reject' readings removed nothing), and there was no posterior fallback anywhere.

What the two lines then did was deeply asymmetric. Both lines bought, admitted and bred their own descendants in all fifteen sessions: 89 of the 90 registered strict-positivity checks pass, the single failure being seed 1 on sitagliptin_mpo, where the second line's two purchases were admitted but never drawn as parents. But an equal field share is not an equal purchase share. The global correlated Thompson buy sent 3,819 of the 4,350 purchases (87.8%) to whichever store held the better molecule, and that store's share climbed monotonically from 77% in the first announcement to 93% in the twenty-ninth. The trailing line took 12.2% of the purchases and produced 1.6% of the realized incumbent progress (0.0855 of 5.2499), contributing exactly zero in eleven of fifteen sessions. Which index led was not fixed: on seed 2 / deco_hop the second line took over and held the incumbent in 28 of 29 announcements.

The registered result measure fell, so the pre-registered scientific falsifier triggered on complete exposure. Realized incumbent-increment mass is 5.249872 against the Parent's 6.079659 (per-cell mean 0.349991 against 0.405311), lower on every seed (1.737977/1.837399/1.674496 against 2.158598/1.967974/1.953087), and the receipt sum and the independent endpoint read agree to the last digit. The complete paired macro panel is 0.558484 against the Parent's 0.613803, a paired delta of -0.055319, negative on all three seeds (-0.084124/-0.026115/-0.055718) against a +0.002 requirement; against the formal Anchor's published 0.607030 the matched-seed difference is -0.048547. The loss concentrates on sitagliptin_mpo (-0.192/-0.086/-0.217) and on seed 0 / deco_hop (-0.255), while median_2 (+0.026/+0.001/+0.017) and zaleplon_mpo (+0.048/0.000/-0.015) were flat to slightly positive. The count of incumbent-improving purchases is unchanged, 256 against 255, so what shrank is the size of the increments, not how often the incumbent moved. Every secondary descent statistic moved the same way: survivor admissions fell from 3,510 to 2,939 with 2,307 residents displaced, and distinct purchases ever drawn as a breeding parent fell from 2,459 to 1,884, leaving 2,316 of the 4,200 non-terminal products terminal against the Parent's 1,741. Delivered diversity, a descriptive check only, also fell rather than rose: typed scaffolds 1,812 to 1,568, generic 1,081 to 965, and nearest-neighbour similarity among non-fragment purchases rose from 0.7487 to 0.7572, with the most common typed scaffold tripling its occurrences from 114 to 358. All fifteen cells are complete and profile-matched: 300 oracle calls, 290 accepted proposals, zero duplicates, zero invalid proposals, exit status ok.

molecular.headline: Flat, halogen-saturated fused aromatics: one scaffold per objective decorated atom-by-atom, with N-halogen and strained-ring liabilities
molecular.overall_character: Across the five objectives the node proposed 4,350 molecules (4,500 records read, including the 150 identical initial records). They are mid-sized, heavily ring-bearing and heavily aromatic: mean SMILES length 42-72 characters, digest ring_closure_rate 0.947-0.982 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.931-0.974, and by RDKit reading 3.0-4.8 rings and 1.9-4.1 aromatic rings per molecule, 24-39 heavy atoms, MW 351-562. The work the optimizer does is almost entirely peripheral: it takes one fused heteroaromatic or bridged polycyclic core per objective and relabels single terminal atoms on it - methyl/ethyl/propyl, OMe, OCH2F, OCHF2, and F/Cl/Br swaps. Halogen presence is extreme (digest halogen_rate 0.908, 0.740, 0.954, 0.208, 0.860) yet not one of the 4,500 records contains a trifluoromethyl group and only 41 contain even a geminal difluoro carbon; fluorine is instead placed on nitrogen or on a benzylic CH2. Nothing carries specified stereochemistry (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five, no '@' in any record) although the best molecules have 1.6-2.4 unassigned tetrahedral centres, and nothing carries a formal charge (charged_rate 0.0011 at most). The top of each score range is one tight family - 85 of the 100 highest-scoring molecules in one set share a single Murcko scaffold - and 138 proposals are degenerate fragments of five heavy atoms or fewer ('O', 'F', 'OF', 'ClNCl'). Medicinal-chemistry quality is poor in a specific way: the cores are reasonable, the decoration is not. N-halogen bonds appear in 1,011 of the 4,350 proposals and dominate the highest-scoring region of two objectives, benzylic bromides and fluoromethyl ethers are common, and one whole top-fifty family is built on a cage whose 3- and 4-membered rings are perceived as aromatic.

per_task.generated_character: A single family of indole/pyrrolo-fused 5-6 bicyclics bearing an aryl carboxamide, grown out of the initial record COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC (0.305). 25 heavy atoms, MW 345-406, three rings all aromatic, logP ~4.3, no stereochemistry, no basic amine, no nitrile (3 of 900 records). The benzo ring carries methyl / methoxy / fluoromethoxy; the amide nitrogen is N-aminated to a 1,1-disubstituted acylhydrazide in 70% of the top fifty (169 of 900 records); the azole nitrogen is N-brominated or N-chlorinated in 50% of the top fifty; a benzylic CH2F / CH2Cl / CH2Br is present in a further 50%. Convergence is extreme: 13 distinct Murcko scaffolds in the top 100 and 85 of those 100 on one scaffold.
liabilities: N-bromo and N-chloro azole nitrogens (n2Br, n2Cl) in half the top fifty - not isolable chemistry
1,1-disubstituted acylhydrazide on an aniline nitrogen, a reactive and toxicophoric amide variant
benzylic fluoromethyl and bromomethyl groups, i.e. latent alkylating agents
fluoromethyl ether OCH2F, hydrolytically unstable
an N-(chloroamino) azole in the last proposals (n2NCl) and an aryl O-S bond (c1OS)
top-fifty QED falls to 0.44 against 0.53 for the whole set, so the score climb moves away from drug-likeness
missing_features: no nitrile anywhere in the high-scoring family (3 of 900 records carry C#N at all)
no pyrazolo-fused N-N bicyclic heteroaromatic; the core stays a single-nitrogen indole-type bicycle
no N-alkyl-N-aryl amide; the amide nitrogen carries NH2 instead of an alkyl group
no single-halogen-only decoration - the top molecules carry two or three halogens including Br and Cl
no carbon-bound basic amine centre in the top fifty (0%); the only NH2 present is the hydrazide nitrogen
no defined stereochemistry anywhere (digest stereocentre_rate 0.0)
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The climb from 0.305 to the best 0.4609 is bought entirely by peripheral single-atom edits to one inherited scaffold: methylate the ether, aminate the amide nitrogen, halogenate the azole nitrogen, move one F around the anilide ring. The gradient is indifferent to halogen identity - CF and CCl variants of the same molecule both score 0.44990, CF and CBr variants both 0.43943 - so most of the budget buys nothing. Everything that loses the fused bicycle collapses: the worst records are bare 'OF', 'ClNCl' and 'O' at 0.0, and the session's own last proposals fall to 0.3065 on an aryl O-S variant (...c1OS) and to 0.0095 on a ring-opened one (C=COC1CC(C=C)C=c2c(nc(Br)n2Cl)=C1C).

per_task.generated_character: The largest and least drug-like set: mean 39.5 heavy atoms, MW 562, 4.8 rings, TPSA 128, QED 0.30. The whole top fifty is one family - a 2,4-disubstituted pyrimidine joined through an N-CH2-O aminal (100% of the top fifty) to a polycyclic cage in which RDKit perceives a 3-membered and a 4-membered aromatic ring (98% and 70% of the top fifty), fused to a 7-membered 1,3-dioxepane. Decoration is fluoromethoxy and difluoromethoxy plus small alkyl. No nitrile (21 of 900 records), no hydrogen-bond donor beyond one, no amide, no basic amine, no stereochemistry. SA score of the top fifty is 5.58 against 4.54 for the set.
liabilities: a cage with aromatic-perceived 3- and 4-membered rings (c4c5c2c4n2oc52), which is not a real substance
an N-CH2-O aminal linker in 100% of the top fifty, hydrolysed in water
fluoromethyl and difluoromethyl ethers throughout
mean MW 562 and TPSA 128 across the set, outside oral drug space
N-halogen bonds in 254 of 900 records even though the top fifty avoid them
missing_features: no nitrile in the top fifty, while the baseline's own high-scoring molecules carry one in 84% of their top fifty
no fused 6-6 diazine (quinazoline-type) bicyclic core - 2 of 900 records contain one
no anilino NH linker; the linker is an N,O-acetal instead of an N-H bridge
no amide or sulfonamide linkage anywhere in the top fifty
no chemically real small ring: the only 3- and 4-membered rings present are aromatic-flagged impossibilities
no stereochemistry, although the top molecules have 1.2 unassigned centres each
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The score range is almost flat where it matters: every fragment, however small, scores exactly 0.5 ('CCF', 'CC', 'OCl', 'C#CC(=C)C=CN'), the median is 0.582, and the entire top fifty lies between 0.6177 and 0.6189 - a span of 0.0012. The gradient rewards keeping the cage-plus-pyrimidine assembly intact and is indifferent to the periphery: OCF against OCHF2, methyl against ethyl against propyl, a 5-, 6- or 7-membered dioxa ring all move the score by less than 0.001. Replacing the aminal O by N (NCNc2...) costs 0.007 and collapsing the cage to a small bicycle (Cc1c(NCN2c3nc(nc(OCF)c3C)C2CF)...) costs 0.031, so the only thing the objective is clearly reading is a motif the generator found once and then stopped changing.

per_task.generated_character: The widest score range of the five (0.00017 to 0.9784). The top fifty is a lipophilic amine chemotype: a cyclobutene-fused dihydronaphthalene carrying a methoxy group (92% of the top fifty contain a 4-membered ring), with a secondary N-methylamine on a benzylic carbon that itself bears bromine - a benzhydryl-type halide in 72% of the top fifty, alkyl halide in 54%. MW 464, logP 5.44, TPSA 45, 2.4 unassigned stereocentres, basic amine in 98% of the top fifty but a ring basic amine in only 2%. Later seed-2 proposals move to a spiro-fused piperidine (CCc1cc2c(c(Cl)c1OC)SC1CCNCC21...) with aminoethoxy and N-bromoaniline decoration, scoring 0.85-0.89.
liabilities: benzhydryl-type bromides and chlorides in 72% of the top fifty: alkylating, not formulable
N-bromo and N-chloro anilines (NBr, NCl) in 178 of 900 records, including the final proposals
a cyclobutene fused to a benzene ring - strained and not a medicinal-chemistry motif
logP 5.4 with MW 464-531 in the top region, outside Lipinski space
an O-S-C-N chain (OSCN) in one of the final molecules
a thiol substituent placed directly on an arene (c1cc(F)cc(S)c1)
missing_features: no basic nitrogen inside a saturated ring in the top fifty (2%), where the comparison baseline's top fifty has 94%
no piperazine anywhere in 900 records, and only 130 records with any ring tertiary amine
no 7-membered-or-larger aliphatic amine ring in the top fifty (4% against the baseline's 96%)
no amide or sulfonamide linker in the high-scoring region
no defined stereochemistry on the two tetrahedral centres every top molecule carries
no polar solubilising group paired with the lipophilic core - the score climb simply strips polarity

per_task.score_gradient_reading: This gradient is a fluorine counter, and the generator found the cheapest way to satisfy it. The top fifty has 90% N-halogen and 62% with three or more fluorines; the bottom fifty has 2% and 6%. Every fluorine the top molecules carry is on nitrogen, on a benzylic CH2, or on a quaternary carbon - never assembled into a trifluoromethyl group. Size is also policed: the inherited large seeds score 1e-45 to 1e-24 and bare atoms ('F', 'Cl') score 1e-26, so the reward sits in a narrow envelope of ~27 heavy atoms with many fluorines. The last proposals of the session show how fragile the family is: the same decorated core scores 0.5036 with a cyclobutenol ring and 0.00028 and 0.047 when that ring is a cumulated-diene carbocycle (C1=C=CC=C1O, C3=C=CC=C3O).

transferable_gaps.evidence: Not one of the 4,500 records read carries a C(F)(F)F group and only 41 carry even a geminal difluoro carbon, although halogen decoration reaches 0.908 and 0.954 of the proposals in two sets. Where a many-fluorine molecule scores well the fluorines are scattered one per heavy atom - on nitrogen, on a benzylic CH2, on a quaternary carbon - as in Cc1ccc(O)c2c1C(F)(CF)Cc1c3c(=N)n(F)c(=O)n(C)c3cn1-2. The same single-atom habit shows up as score-neutral churn elsewhere: the same core with CH2F and with CH2Cl scores identically (0.44990 twice), and with CH2F and CH2Br identically (0.43943 twice).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator cannot assemble a multi-atom substituent in one move; it only relabels single terminal atoms, so no trihalomethyl or other geminally substituted carbon ever appears.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add a substituent-level move that inserts or deletes a whole named group as one unit from a small medicinal-chemistry library (trifluoromethyl, cyano, sulfonamide, trifluoromethoxy, acetamide), instead of only point-mutating one atom label. A capability that needs three coordinated edits to appear, each of which is neutral or harmful alone, is unreachable for a per-atom operator.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 1,011 of the 4,350 proposals contain an N-F, N-Cl or N-Br bond; they make up 90% of the top fifty in one set and 50% in another (n(F) imides such as Cn1c(=O)n(F)c(=N)..., N-brominated azoles such as ...n2Br, N-chloro anilines such as c(NCl)). A further 169 proposals in one set carry a 1,1-disubstituted acylhydrazide formed by aminating an anilide nitrogen (C(=O)N(N)c3ccccc3), and element swaps also produce an aryl O-S bond (...c1OS) and an O-S-C-N chain (OSCN). None of these are isolable substances, and nothing in the loop removes them.
transferable_gaps.gap: Element substitution is not constrained by what the receiving atom can actually bond: the generator freely makes nitrogen-halogen, nitrogen-nitrogen and oxygen-sulfur bonds, and these dominate its own highest-scoring molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Apply an element-compatibility rule to the atom-substitution operator - halogens and chalcogens attach to carbon, not to nitrogen or to each other - and reject heteroatom-heteroatom products at proposal time. Otherwise a scoring function that only counts atoms or fingerprints will keep steering the search into reagent chemistry, and the population's whole top band becomes unusable output.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five objectives, and no record among 4,500 contains an '@'. Yet the top fifty molecules carry 1.2 to 2.4 unassigned tetrahedral centres each by RDKit perception - for instance CNC(C1=CC2=C(CC1)c1cccc(OC)c12)C(Br)c1cc(F)cc(F)c1 has two, and CCCc1c(OCC)ccc2c1N1C(C)CC(=O)N(C)CC(=O)N(C)CCC1c1ccccc1O2 has two ring-fusion centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never specifies stereochemistry; every molecule it emits is a flat graph, including the ones whose ring fusions and benzylic centres create real stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Either carry stereochemistry in the representation and add a move that sets or inverts a centre, or declare the search explicitly achiral and prefer scaffolds without unassigned centres. As it stands the generator cannot distinguish two molecules that differ only in configuration, so it cannot climb any objective, filter or docking term that depends on three-dimensional fit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In one set 90 of 900 records contain a 3-membered ring and 144 a 4-membered ring, and 98% / 70% of that set's top fifty are a single cage, CCc1nc(NCOc2c3c(c4c5c2c4n2oc52)OCCCO3)c(C)c(OC(F)F)n1, whose 3- and 4-membered rings are perceived as aromatic; its SA score is 5.58 against 4.54 for the set. Another set has 87 records with a cumulated double bond (digest cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1), e.g. Cn1c(=O)c2c(SC(CF)=C(F)C(F)CF)n(C3=C=CC=C3O)nc2n(C)c1=O, and a third shows a benzo ring degraded to a cyclopentadiene (...C1=CC=CC1O2).
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-forming recombination produces ring systems that cannot exist - including 3- and 4-membered rings carrying aromatic flags and cumulated double bonds inside rings - and nothing filters them out, so one of them became an entire high-scoring plateau.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Constrain the ring-closing and ring-fusing moves to produce 5-, 6- and 7-membered rings with legal unsaturation, and reject small aromatic-flagged rings, cumulated in-ring unsaturation and bridgeheads that imply impossible geometry. An unfiltered cage that happens to satisfy a similarity term will hold a bounded population's whole top band and the search will spend its remaining budget decorating something no chemist can order.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Nitriles appear in 21, 6, 4, 3 and 3 of the 900 records per set, and the only seed that contained one is COc1cc(OC)c2c(-c3cccc(-c4ccc(C#N)cc4)c3)cc(=O)oc2c1; sulfonamides appear three to six times per set except in the one set where the seed's own sulfonyl fragment survives (CC1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1, 101 records there). Benzodioxole never appears in 4,500 records, nor does any pyrazolo-fused pyrimidinone, and a fused 6-6 diazine bicyclic appears twice in the set whose comparison baseline carried it 129 times.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates no functional group it was not given: its group inventory is the seed pool's inventory, re-decorated with single atoms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Give the proposal step a source of new groups that does not depend on the initial pool - a fragment library, a reaction-template expansion, or a retrieval step over known chemistry - because crossover between stored parents can only recombine what the pool already contains, and a bounded population loses rare groups permanently once their carriers are evicted.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring tertiary amines appear in 24, 12, 130, 258 and 16 of the 900 records per set, and a saturated piperazine ring in 5 of all 4,500. In the set where a basic centre clearly pays, 98% of the top fifty have a basic amine but only 2% have it inside a ring and 4% inside a ring of seven or more atoms - the best molecule is an acyclic N-methylamine, CNC(C1=CC2=C(CC1)c1cccc(OC)c12)C(Br)c1cc(F)cc(F)c1 - whereas the comparison baseline's published top fifty on the same objective carries a ring tertiary amine in 94% of cases and a 7-or-larger amine ring in 96%, and reaches a higher best score. Where this generator does reach a ring amine it is a late spiro piperidine, CCc1cc2c(c(Cl)c1OC)SC1CCNCC21c1cc(F)c(OCCN)c(NBr)c1.
transferable_gaps.gap: Basic nitrogen is produced almost exclusively as an acyclic or exocyclic amine; the generator rarely builds a saturated nitrogen heterocycle and does not retain one in its highest-scoring molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Add moves that cyclise an existing amine into a saturated ring and that expand or contract such a ring by one atom, and keep ring-amine carriers in memory rather than letting peripheral-atom variants of one acyclic winner crowd them out. The capability to place a basic centre inside a ring is a different move from placing a basic atom at all, and only the second one is currently present.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 138 of the 4,350 proposals have five or fewer heavy atoms, in 86 distinct forms - 'C' ten times, 'F' seven, 'CO' five, 'CF' five, 'O', 'OF', 'ClNCl', 'FF', 'CCl' - and they score the floor of their range every time (0.0, 1.1e-26, 0.5, 0.0033).
transferable_gaps.gap: A measurable share of proposals are not molecules: single atoms and two-atom fragments that consume evaluations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Gate proposals on a minimum heavy-atom count and on at least one ring before spending an evaluation, and treat a fragment-producing crossover as a failed attempt to be retried rather than as a candidate. Roughly three per cent of the evaluation budget is currently returned as information about atoms.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
